answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The lotus multiplier is published, charged in cedar, and orchard lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3090 identities would post 1942 proofs and burn roughly 41 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
